props.description: Every workflow in the bundled sdlc pack, what it produces and when to use it.

itself is a graph of the stage workflows below. Triage picks a route; investigate or plan runs when the route needs it; then the delivery rounds implement, open a draft pull request, review it through specialist lenses, fix the findings and wait for CI. Stages hand each other files in

lists every workflow by when to use it. To ask a question or explore the codebase, ask in chat; no workflow is needed.

Grounds an issue or request against the current repository before spending on it, then takes the least speculative path: investigate an unknown cause, plan an undecided shape, deliver an implementation-ready work order, continue an open PR that already carries the outcome, or stop when no work remains. Every actionable path ends in the same reviewed delivery tail as
: A GitHub issue or request should go from a current-truth check to a reviewed PR. This is your default for bugs, features, and enhancements.

: A PR marked ready for review once its review passes, for the merge queue to judge its CI, or an explained stop, with a PR it opened left in draft. The stop says whether no work is owed (the outcome already holds, or an investigation found the cause outside this repository) or the requested work was not done and why. The run's result says whether it delivered; when it did not, such as on a question triage or the plan could not settle, an unrooted cause, or a delivery that ended not ready,
. The workflow never merges. Merge a pull request it opened yourself; the merge queue merges only what the build queue finished.
has delivery finish that open PR whichever route reaches delivery; a run that stops before delivery leaves it as it was, and a run whose triage names a different PR to continue fails before delivery.
Delivering one part of a multi-part plan
: When an approved plan splits the work into several PRs, tell the run which part it delivers and which contract items each part owns, quoting each item as the contract states it:

archon workflow run archon-ship --branch feat/export-csv-api \
  --input part='{"delivers":1,"parts":[{"part":1,"items":["The API returns CSV."]},{"part":2,"items":["The console offers a CSV download.","Users can export their data as CSV."]}]}' \
  "#142"
The review then treats an item that only later parts list as deferred: it is neither a blocking finding nor a discovery, and the PR says

instead of closing the issue. The required outcome is an item like any other, so list it under the part that completes it, as the example does with "Users can export their data as CSV." An item the input lists under no part is still reviewed as part of this PR, and the review still reports a change that contradicts a later part. The run never works out part ownership from the plan's prose; without this input, the PR is reviewed against the whole contract.

Reconciles an issue, plan, or request with the current code, tracker history, and stated direction, judges whether it is a contract a run can start from, then routes it to investigate, plan, deliver, split, or no action.
: An item may be stale or may prescribe an unverified solution, and you want to know what it needs next before paying for the work.
: A verdict with the recommended next step. It leaves the checkout unchanged. Pass
to write the derived labels to the issue. An item that is blocked or needs contract work ends the run not ready, with the question in the verdict;
The standing front of the pack, started by trigger bindings on issue and label events rather than by hand. A script checks whether the issue's author is on the project's maintainer list (
) before any model reads the text. A maintainer's issue is triaged and gets a route label; an outside issue gets
and starts no agent until a listed maintainer adds
: You want new issues triaged as they arrive without letting anyone who can open an issue spend tokens.
runs it by hand and binds it.
) holding its trust, stage, triage fields, and history, and the labels that mirror it.
The stage after intake, started by a schedule binding. Each run claims the triaged item that sorts first, or the issue
names, runs one round on it from a brief, and reads how the round ended. A round is

without its triage, since intake already triaged the item: the queue's route agent declares the route and checks that triage's verdict still holds. A clear case acts on its own: the item is done when its pull request is reviewed Ready at its head, unless only a check no round can run remains, which it asks for once at that head (a maintainer's

answer also hands it to the merge queue, whose gate still checks it), and a correctable finding or a stop the issue already answers starts the item's next round at once (never when the pull request changed nothing material since its last review), as a detached

run on the same run config. An unclear one, a correction that would add machinery the issue does not ask for, a Ready pull request waiting only on a check no round can run, or several rounds that each find new defects, pauses as one attention item with the agent's recommendation and declared choices; the answer is written into the issue body as a dated "Current scope" section.
: You want triaged issues worked to reviewed pull requests without answering every routine stop yourself.
runs it by hand and binds it.
: Reviewed pull requests, the queue's record on each work item (
: status, rounds and decisions), and attention items for the decisions that need a person.

The stage after the build queue, started by a schedule binding. Each run claims the items whose pull requests the build queue made ready, and one agent sweeps them: it orders them, merges each Ready, green pull request that merges cleanly into the base branch, hands back to the build queue what it can fix (a conflict, a stale or missing verdict, a review thread that raises a defect, red the change caused), and never pushes or waits for CI itself. Every merge goes through a gate script that refuses unless the review verdict says Ready for the head, CI is green there, the base branch's CI is not red and the head contains the base branch or merges into it cleanly (open review threads are the sweep's judgment), and merges pinned to that head. The base branch's CI on a merge is the next sweep's first fact. An unclear pull request, such as a very large change, is asked as soon as its review is Ready, as a
attention item with the agent's recommendation and declared choices. A red base branch raises a
. A run raises at most one attention item: the red base branch first, otherwise the first pull request the sweep asked about; a later sweep decides the rest again.
: You want reviewed, green pull requests merged without merging each by hand, while changes that need a person still wait for one.
runs it by hand and binds it.
: Merged pull requests, the queue's record on each work item (
: status and decisions), and attention items for the decisions that need a person.

Drains the discoveries finished runs recorded outside their own scope. One agent verifies each one against the default branch, merges duplicates across runs and with earlier decisions, and decides: file an issue with a full brief, track it on the open issue that already covers it, drop it with a reason, ask a maintainer, or wait when the code it is about is still on an open pull request, so a later pass decides it after that pull request merges or closes. Scripts perform only the writes it declared.
: Runs keep finding defects outside their change and nobody reads their
runs it by hand and binds it. Naming its binding in the merge queue's
input also starts a pass after each sweep that merged a pull request.
: Filed issues and evidence comments, and one state document per drained run (
) recording which of its records were decided and any question asked with its answer, so a record is decided once.
Files the issues a large item splits into, when triage routed the item

. A large item, such as a PRD, an epic or a bundle of tasks, is built as one work item by default; triage splits it only when building it whole would not work, and says why. Triage passes a PRD only when it states a hypothesis, the signal that proves or disproves it with the command that measures it, and a threshold and window; otherwise it asks for that contract work. One agent checks triage's reason first and can hand the item back to the build queue whole, with why. Otherwise it files only the piece that comes next, each issue a contract of its own: a PRD's current phase, an epic's current increment, or every task of a bundle. Later phases are recorded on the item, each with what the earlier work must show before it is filed. A script files each issue once and comments the list and the plan on the item. A PRD is labelled
and stays open; an epic stays open until its increments merge; a bundle is closed.
: Your issues include PRDs, epics or lists of tasks too large to build as one work item. Add the binding the SDLC pack README's "Split queue" section shows; the pack installs none. By hand:
: The filed issues, which come back through intake, a comment on the item listing them, and the queue's record on its work item (
: status, kind and filed issues, or the route when the item was built whole).

across every registered project: each merged worktree goes, with its local branch, including a branch the worktree adopted rather than created. Git ancestry or patch equivalence proves a merge without a pull request; otherwise the branch's merged pull request does. Cleanup retains remote branches with a logged warning, including with force. Enable GitHub's
setting for merged pull requests, or follow

also removes worktrees whose pull request was closed.

: You run Archon without a server, whose cleanup schedule already does this, and merged worktrees pile up. Add the schedule binding the SDLC pack README's "Worktree cleanup" section shows; the pack installs none.
: The cleanup report on the node's output. It changes no code.
Establishes the proven causal chain for a bug, unexplained behavior, or open question, down to the root cause whose fix prevents the symptom.
: The cause is not yet known and you want it proven before anyone writes a fix.
archon workflow run archon-investigate "Why does the workflow list spin forever when no workflows exist?"
: An evidence-backed report a fixer or planner can act on, with a verdict:
(a change is owed here and the fix is decided),
(no change is owed in this repository), or
(the cause is not established yet). The repository is left as it was found.

Turns decided intent, such as a feature request, an investigation report, or an idea, into an implementable plan: the chosen approach with rejected alternatives, verifiable steps, and the validation that proves it.
: You know what to build but not how.
archon workflow run archon-plan "Add CSV export to the reports page"

to build on a prior investigation report. The repository is left as it was found. Before it stops to ask a question, it checks whether the work order, the issue's comments, a project document, or a ruling your maintainers recorded in
already answers it; review synthesis does the same before it returns

. An addition that leaves every existing value meaning what it meant before is the plan's call, not a person's: the plan lists it under contract additions and the pull request body flags it for the reviewer. Changing what an existing value means, removing something shipped, or changing a persisted shape still stops to ask: the run ends not ready with the questions in the plan;
that answers them. The SDLC pack README's sidecar section describes the rulings document.
Implements a change and keeps working until it is complete and the project's own checks pass. It commits as it goes and opens no PR.
: The work is decided and needs building: a plan, review findings, a CI failure, or a plain description.
archon workflow run archon-implement --branch feat/export-csv "Implement the plan in .archon/plans/csv-export.md"

Opens a pull request for the committed work on the current branch. It neither merges the base nor runs checks: CI judges the pushed head. It uses the repository's PR template when one exists, pushes the branch, and reads the created PR back to verify it. It references a linked issue with
, never a closing keyword, because no review has judged the work yet.
: A branch has committed work and needs a PR. Run it with
from the checkout that holds the branch.
: A pull request, draft unless you pass
. It never sweeps in unrelated changes, never rebases, and never force-pushes.

The delivery tail, in capped rounds: implement the work with focused checks on what it changes, push and open (or update) a draft PR, and review it, with a structure pass beside the review that looks for a smaller shape; the next round's implementer adopts or declines its findings together with the review's. Once a round's review passes and the structure pass names nothing, an agent reads the checks once and hands the PR off ready without waiting for CI (the full validation): pending checks and red outside the change are the merge queue's to judge before it merges. A project with no CI gets the full validation from that agent instead. Review findings, smaller shapes, a check already red because of the change, and a conflict with the base go back to the implementer for another round (it merges the base on a conflict, never rebasing), up to four rounds. Each correction is reviewed on its delta, leaving out code a merge of the base brought in, by the general code reviewer, which judges every prior finding, plus any lens the route agent adds because the delta reaches new ground in its area. Any other ending is not ready, with its reason. When the work requires content in the PR description, such as benchmark results, the round publishes it into a marked section of the description before review reads the PR, leaving the rest of the description as written. Finally it updates the PR description and relays any discoveries. The description closes its issue (
) only when the last review's contract coverage marks the required outcome and every acceptance item met and no dated ruling on the issue keeps it open; otherwise it says

and lists what is left or names the ruling. The run's outcome lists the contract items left open; a ruling that keeps the issue open is named only in the description. Before merging, the merge queue rechecks the keyword against the review's stamped coverage and the issue's latest ruling, and corrects it in either direction.
continues that open PR instead of opening one.
opens the PR from that branch instead of the checkout's, or updates the open PR that already has it as its head.
delivers one part of a multi-part plan, as described for

for another batch of rounds on the same PR. It never pauses for approval of a ready PR; your gate is PR review and merge.
: The work is decided, for example an approved plan, and should become a reviewed, ready-to-merge PR.
archon workflow run archon-deliver --branch feat/export-csv "Deliver the plan in .archon/plans/csv-export.md"
: A PR marked ready for review, with one canonical review comment.

Reviews a change through specialist lenses and produces one evidence-based verdict. Every round, a quick route agent picks the lenses the change earns: seams (on unless the change touches no type, contract, state or boundary), code (which uses the configured
model tier), tests, errors, docs, and ux (for a change a person sees or does in a browser: it starts the app and uses the change, on the
overrides its errors call. A continuation (

) reviews the correction delta only (code a merge of the base brought in is left out). The general code reviewer always runs and judges whether each prior finding was resolved or validly declined; every lens that raised a blocker the previous round left open runs again to verify its findings and check the fix for new defects in its area; the route agent adds another lens only when the delta reaches new ground in its area. When the verdict is not ready, three independent verifiers judge each blocking finding, and one that at least two of them reject is demoted: to a discovery when it predates the change, to disproved when it is not real. Findings from the contract check are never demoted. The review also holds the change to its stated contract, taken from the PR description or a work order you pass: each stated acceptance item and invariant is met with cited evidence or raised as a blocking finding.
reviews one part of a multi-part plan, as described for
: A PR or your working diff needs judging. It never edits code. On a PR it posts or edits its review comment; it never changes the PR's draft state.
archon workflow run archon-review --input scope=87 --branch fix/login-redirect
with the PR's head branch for a same-repository PR.
reuses an existing healthy worktree without advancing it. Before rerunning, locate it with
and check for local changes. Only when clean, run

with the PR's actual values. Verify its HEAD equals the current PR head SHA before rerunning. Stop on local changes, divergence or an ahead checkout and reconcile them before retrying. For a fork PR, fetch its head into the launch repository first, then start a fresh review branch at that commit:

git fetch <fork-clone-url> <PR-head-ref>
archon workflow run archon-review --input scope=<PR-URL> --branch <fresh-review-branch> --from <PR-head-SHA>
Use the fork's actual clone URL, head ref and full head SHA, and choose a review branch absent locally, on the configured remote and from existing worktrees.
only applies to a new branch;

alone cannot resolve a fork-only ref and would create it from the base. The review reads the checkout. If its commit differs from the PR head, the run still reviews the checkout but refuses to publish, naming both commits.
: A synthesized review report. When reviewing a PR whose head is the reviewed commit, the report is posted as one comment and edited in place on re-review. Empty
selects the current branch's open PR first, otherwise the working diff. A Ready verdict leaves a draft PR a draft; take it out of draft on the forge.

Keeps one dependency current. It grounds the update against the repository (locked version, blast radius, breaking changes that touch real usage), then either stops with the reason or takes the bump through the reviewed delivery tail.
: A dependency update or security advisory should become a reviewed PR. One target per run.
archon workflow run archon-upkeep "Address the undici advisory"
: A PR marked ready for review, or an explained stop when the locked version is already current.

Judges the tests in each factory pull request merged since a date, one
run per pull request, and records

: how many tests it added or changed, and how many of them protect nothing on their own merits, as tests in the suite rather than against what the pull request promised. Redundancy is judged against the tests the judge is shown: the pull request's changed tests and the files that hold them. Both counts name the judge's identity. The judge reads each pull request's changed files and the text of each file holding test code through the forge plugin's
; a pull request whose files the plugin cannot read is skipped.
